circuit: copy of testcase/test26/test26.v (1629 gates, 205 DFFs, 42 XNOR)
purpose: Transform routing: a TARGETED gate-type conversion followed by a WHOLE-DESIGN basis remap, then an optimisation that must respect the basis. The catalog carries a 'targeted gate-type conversion vs convert_basis' block for exactly this pair.

lines.prompt: How many XNOR cells does this design carry?
lines.why_correct: A count of one named type.
lines.why_hard: Baseline for line 5; count_gates would return the whole breakdown.

lines.prompt: Take the XNOR cells and build each one out of NOR logic instead. Leave everything else alone.
lines.why_correct: Only the XNOR cells are named, so this is the targeted decomposition, not a whole-design remap.
lines.why_hard: 'Build each one out of NOR logic' reads exactly like a basis instruction; only 'Leave everything else alone' holds the scope down. convert_basis would rewrite all 1629 gates instead of 42.

lines.prompt: How many XNOR cells are left?
lines.why_correct: Current inventory of one type after a transform.
lines.why_hard: Catalog 'count_type vs delta_count after a transform': delta_count would report how many were converted (42) rather than how many remain (0). Both are plausible numbers here.

lines.prompt: Now bring the whole thing down to NAND and NOT only.
lines.why_correct: 'The whole thing' is a whole-design basis remap.
lines.why_hard: The mirror of line 4 on the same design: one is targeted, one is global. A router that treats both the same fails one of them.

lines.prompt: Keeping the netlist NAND and NOT only, squeeze the critical path as short as you can.
lines.why_hard: The basis is named in the request, so this is not a memory test. Dropping the basis parameter still routes to minimize_depth and still reports an improved depth -- but the netlist leaves NAND/NOT, violating the constraint the sentence states outright (Q&A A63). Only the params reveal it.

lines.mechanism: sentence weight pulls to the design-wide reading
lines.why_hard: 'Taking the netlist as a whole' sits in the focus position and pulls toward global_max_depth (58 here against the correct 11); the scope survives only in the trailing 'that ends at n8[0]'. Verified to beat the router on test81 line 8 and, in the same shape, on test82 line 3 and test83 line 5. A mis-route returns a different number, so the error shows up in the answer.
lines.prompt: Taking the netlist as a whole, how deep does the logic that ends at n8[0] run?

notes: Values: XNOR before=42, after the targeted conversion=0.
Line 7 is scored on params: minimize_depth without basis=NAND_NOT breaks the constraint set in line 6 while still looking like a success.
Optimisability was verified on this circuit: after to_basis(NAND_NOT) the depth goes 58 -> 112 and minimize_depth then reaches 21, so line 7 has real headroom.

Every line is self-contained: nothing refers to an earlier turn. The agent sends no conversation history to the model (system = catalog, user = the current line only), so anaphoric wording would test dialogue memory rather than routing.

Every scored failure in this case is a DEFINITE routing error: the wrong choice yields a different number, a different answer shape, or a materially different netlist. Parameters whose values are interchangeable in practice (verify_equivalence against=original vs last_loaded on a single load, insert_buffers mode omitted when fanout is the default) were removed, because a mis-route there changes nothing observable.
